A 20-year assessment history for all eighteen Monty Tech member towns (p149), transposed so towns are columns and in a non-alphabetical order that matches no other table in the report. Reading it by column position without checking the header assigns another town's history to Lunenburg.

Monty Tech's per-program enrollment split by gender for all twenty vocational programs is a complete dataset that exists ONLY as parentheticals at the end of prose paragraphs (p126-133) -- no heading, no table, invisible to any search for a table title.

The Special Services report (p102) gives out-of-district special education PLACEMENT COUNTS by type -- 14 students: 2 collaborative, 8 day, 4 residential, against 19 the prior year. That is the count the budget documents never publish, sitting in a narrative section of the town report.

Town Clock Winders is a formally appointed office with six named appointees (p13), alongside Pound Keeper, Fence Viewers (listed as 'Vacancies'), Field Driver, Dam Keeper and Assistant Dam Keeper, and seven Public Weighers appointed specifically for P.J. Keating Co.

The report contains at least three internal figure disagreements that a reader would only find by cross-checking: the fire department's four call categories sum to 2143 against a stated 2107 (p79); PEG access revenue is $107,849.80 in one sentence and $107,889.80 two pages later (p68/p69); and Monty Tech's FY14 total expenditure is $24,785,280 on p142 and $24,785,240 on p143.

Motor vehicle excise receivables are still being carried back to the levy of 2003, and personal property receivables back to the levy of 1998 (p43-44) -- a twenty-year uncollected tail listed year by year.

Five of the report's biggest financial tables (capital project funds p34, trust funds p37-39, debt repayment schedule p41-42, receivables summary p43-45, Monty Tech balance sheet p140) come out of the text layer TRANSPOSED -- each column collapsed into one run-on line and the row labels stranded at the bottom.
